title: Cofinal restriction of relative join cocones and its dual
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], join slices of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], and inner fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $j:A\hookrightarrow B$ be a full subcategory of a small quasicategory, and suppose that for each $b\in B$ the coherent comma quasicategory of arrows $b\to j(a)$ is weakly contractible. Let $p:C\to D$ be an inner fibration of quasicategories and $u:B\to C$ a functor. Define $(C_{u/})_k$ to consist of maps $B\star\Delta^k\to C$ restricting to $u$, with restriction operators, and analogously for the other coslices. Then
$$C_{u/}\longrightarrow C_{uj/}\times_{D_{puj/}}D_{pu/}$$
is a trivial Kan fibration, so every prescribed boundary and every prescribed base simplex lift exactly. The hypothesis holds in particular if the inclusion $j$ admits a left adjoint, meaning a coherent functor $R:B\to A$ with coherently natural equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_A(Rb,a)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_B(b,j a)$. Dually, if each comma quasicategory of arrows $j(a)\to b$ is weakly contractible, restriction induces a trivial Kan fibration
$$C_{/u}\longrightarrow C_{/uj}\times_{D_{/puj}}D_{/pu}.$$
The dual hypothesis holds when $A$ chooses one initial object in each component of $B$. Weak contractibility means weak homotopy equivalence to a point; a trivial Kan fibration lifts every boundary inclusion, including dimension zero. There are no colimit or limit existence assumptions.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, printed p.336 (active-subslice cofinal restriction) and p.341 (initial output components), using HTT Theorem 4.1.3.1 (comma criterion), Proposition 4.1.1.3(4) (cofinal monomorphisms are right anodyne), and Proposition 2.1.2.5 (relative coslice restriction is a trivial Kan fibration), with the opposite versions. The two orientations are specified explicitly. September 18, 2017 edition inspected online. WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: The full inclusion $j$ is degreewise injective. Interpret its coherent comma as the arrow pullback $(b\downarrow j)=\{b\}\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_1}A$, with the constant simplicial point at $b$. The hypothesis of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-mono-right-anodyne] is therefore satisfied, so $j$ is right anodyne. If $A$ is empty and $B$ has a vertex, this hypothesis fails because the comma is empty; if $B$ is empty, $j$ is the identity of the empty simplicial set.

source.place: Remark 7.2.3.2 (right-cofinal arrow-comma model), Theorem 7.2.3.1 and Proposition 7.2.1.3; equivalently HTT Theorem 4.1.3.1 and Proposition 4.1.1.3(4), printed pp.236 and 223.

proof.text:
Fix $n\geq1$ and a lifting square for the displayed restriction map against $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$. Unwinding the join-slice definitions, the square supplies a map $A\star\Delta^n\to C$, a map $B\star\partial\Delta^n\to C$, and a base map $B\star\Delta^n\to D$; on $A\star\partial\Delta^n$ the two $C$-maps agree, and the map from $A\star\Delta^n$ to $C$ lies over the restriction of the base map. This is precisely the lifting problem for $p:C\to D$ with source inclusion
$$i_n=(A\star\Delta^n)\amalg_{A\star\partial\Delta^n}(B\star\partial\Delta^n)\longrightarrow B\star\Delta^n.$$
Since $j$ is right anodyne, [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones] says that $i_n$ is inner anodyne. The join and pullback identifications here are degreewise, so the prescribed boundary is retained exactly.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, printed p. 336; unpack the relative coslice lifting square and apply the join pushout-anodyne lemma

proof.text: The map $p$ is an inner fibration by hypothesis, so it has the right lifting property against each inner horn. The class of maps against which an inner fibration lifts is closed under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts: pushout lifting is obtained by composing with the pushout universal property, transfinite lifting is obtained successively at successor stages and by the colimit property at limit stages, and retract lifting is obtained by inserting the retract maps. Therefore $p$ lifts against the inner-anodyne map $i_n$. The resulting map $B\star\Delta^n\to C$ restricts to the prescribed $C$-maps and projects to the prescribed base map, hence is the required $n$-simplex lift.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, printed p. 336; Proposition 2.1.2.5 lifting argument for an inner-fibration target

proof.text: For $n=0$, the same construction uses $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$ and the inner-anodyne inclusion $(A\star\Delta^0)\amalg_A B\to B\star\Delta^0$ supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones]. The inner-fibration lifting property gives a vertex of $C_{u/}$ above every compatible vertex of the fiber product. Thus the restriction map is surjective on vertices. Together with the positive-dimensional boundary lifts of steps 2--3, this is exactly the definition of a trivial Kan fibration in [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration].

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, printed p. 336; dimension-zero clause of Proposition 2.1.2.5

proof.text: For the dual slice assertion define $X^{\mathrm{op}}$ by replacing each simplicial operator $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ by $a\mapsto n-\alpha(m-a)$. Reversal sends $\Lambda_i^n$ to $\Lambda_{n-i}^n$, so it preserves inner fibrations and takes right anodyne maps to left anodyne maps. It also preserves boundary inclusions. Reversing barycentric coordinates gives $|X^{\mathrm{op}}|\cong|X|$, so weak contractibility is preserved. In the arrow-pullback comma, reversal and interchange of the endpoints identify $(b\downarrow j^{\mathrm{op}})$ with $(j\downarrow b)^{\mathrm{op}}$. Thus [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-mono-right-anodyne] applies to $j^{\mathrm{op}}$, which is a full degreewise inclusion, and makes $j^{\mathrm{op}}$ right anodyne. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones] to this map and $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$. It gives the inner-anodyne map $(A^{\mathrm{op}}\star\Delta^n)\amalg_{A^{\mathrm{op}}\star\partial\Delta^n}(B^{\mathrm{op}}\star\partial\Delta^n)\to B^{\mathrm{op}}\star\Delta^n$. Reversing its simplices gives the inner-anodyne map $(\Delta^n\star A)\amalg_{\partial\Delta^n\star A}(\partial\Delta^n\star B)\to\Delta^n\star B$, because reversal interchanges the ordered join blocks and preserves pushouts degreewise. A boundary square for $C_{/u}\to C_{/uj}\times_{D_{/puj}}D_{/pu}$ is precisely a map from this pushout to $C$ over a specified map $\Delta^n\star B\to D$. The inner fibration $p$ lifts it by the closure argument of step 3. For $n=0$ its source is $(\Delta^0\star A)\amalg_A B$, giving vertex surjectivity. For all $n>0$ it gives the prescribed boundary lifts, so [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration] gives the asserted trivial Kan fibration.

source.place: Opposite of Lemma 2.1.2.3 and Proposition 2.1.2.5, printed pp.62-63; explicit reversal of horns, joins and boundary squares.

proof.text: For the left-adjoint special case, [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-adjoint-criterion] supplies the coherent unit $\eta:1_B\to jR$ and counit $\epsilon:Rj\to1_A$ and their triangle homotopies from the assumed natural mapping-space equivalences. Fix $b$ and put $Q=(b\downarrow j)$, with projection $v:Q\to A$ and tautological coherent transformation $\alpha:\Delta_Q b\to jv$. It contains the vertex $q_b=(Rb,\eta_b)$. For an object $(a,\alpha_a)$, the arrow from $q_b$ to this object has underlying arrow $h_a=\epsilon_a\circ R(\alpha_a):Rb\to a$. Its comma triangle is $j(h_a)\eta_b\simeq j(\epsilon_a)\eta_{ja}\alpha_a\simeq\alpha_a$: the first homotopy is naturality of $\eta$, and the second is the triangle identity for $j$. Apply these same coherent transformations to the entire diagram $v,\alpha$, rather than only to its vertices; their coherent naturality supplies an edge $\Delta_Q q_b\to1_Q$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,Q)$, hence a simplicial map $Q\times\Delta^1\to Q$ from the constant map to the identity. By [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-cylinder] its realization is a homotopy between these maps. Thus $|Q|$ is homotopy equivalent to a point, so $Q$ is weakly contractible for every $b$. Step 1 and the boundary construction therefore apply. This also proves that a right adjoint to $j$ supplies the dual comma hypothesis: the assumed mapping equivalences reverse to the left-adjoint equivalences for $j^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the comma identification of step 5 identifies the resulting contractions with contractions of $(j\downarrow b)^{\mathrm{op}}$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, printed p.336: the active-subslice inclusion admits a left adjoint. The displayed unit-counit contraction supplies the omitted comma-contractibility argument.

proof.text: Finally suppose $A$ is the full subcategory choosing one initial vertex $t_i$ in each component $B_i$ of $B$. For $b\in B_i$, the presheaves on $A$ given by $a\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_B(ja,b)$ and $a\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_A(a,t_i)$ have contractible values at $a=t_i$ and empty values on every other component. The first assertion is initiality of $t_i$ in $B_i$; the second uses fullness, and maps between distinct components have no vertices and hence form the empty simplicial set. Both presheaves map naturally to the presheaf which is a point on component $i$ and empty elsewhere. These maps are pointwise equivalences, hence equivalences by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Thus $a\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_B(ja,b)$ is represented by $t_i$. The right-adjoint direction of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-adjoint-criterion] assembles these representing objects into a right adjoint to $j$. The last conclusion of step 6 proves the dual comma hypothesis and step 5 proves the dual restriction assertion. If $B$ is empty there are no $b$ to test and both restrictions are identities; the representation argument imposes no nonemptiness assumption.
